Article Title: 'No one could tell them no': Jensen Huang's daughter Madison, son-in-law played big role in Nvidia's response to Megaspeed probe - report
Article Text:
Huang's daughter shaped Nvidia's response to Megaspeed probe

Madison Huang took charge of communications response

Caprez's growing role in Nvidia's Asia business

US investigation into Megaspeed and alleged

chip diversion

Jensen Huang summoned to testify before US Congress

Alice Huang faces scrutiny in Singapore

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang's daughter, Madison Huang, played a significant role in managing the company's public response to scrutiny over its business relationship with Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed, which is at the centre of a US investigation into the alleged diversion of advanced chips to China, according to a Financial Times report.Madison Huang, a senior director of product marketing at Nvidia, took on responsibilities beyond her formal role, helping direct the company's response to growing media scrutiny of Megaspeed, three people familiar with the matter told the Financial Times.Her involvement, along with the role played by her husband and fellow Nvidia executive Nico Caprez, is expected to attract greater scrutiny as the company's board investigates the circumstances surrounding its relationship with Megaspeed.The developments come days after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO following reports of alleged relationships with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who US intelligence officials suspect of having links to Chinese espionage efforts, and a subordinate at Nvidia.According to the Financial Times, Madison Huang began involving herself directly in Nvidia's communications strategy in autumn 2025, when the company's dealings with Megaspeed started attracting media attention.She had privately hired crisis public relations firm Heller for the Huang family in spring 2025. The firm, known for handling high-profile individuals involved in sexual misconduct controversies, later began working directly for Nvidia.Around the same time, Madison Huang temporarily excluded one of Nvidia's senior corporate communications executives from the internal group discussing how to respond to questions about the company's chip sales to Megaspeed. The group that remained involved in preparing responses included Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter.One Nvidia colleague described the influence exercised by Madison Huang and Caprez within the company, telling the Financial Times, “They had a lot of power and influence and were allowed to operate unchecked. No one could tell them ‘no’ or put them in their place," as cited by the Financial Times.The report also raised questions about the company's governance, with current and former employees expressing concerns over Jensen Huang's decision to place family members in senior positions at Nvidia, even before his departure.Caprez, whom Madison Huang recently married, also assumed a broader role in Nvidia's international business as scrutiny of Megaspeed intensified.A fellow Nvidia executive, Caprez joined the company in 2024 and was promoted in autumn 2025 to a director-level position overseeing its international cloud computing partnerships in Asia.Two people familiar with the matter told the Financial Times that Caprez had travelled to Asia to oversee deals with cloud providers and had been involved in transactions with regional cloud partners months before his formal promotion. Megaspeed was among Nvidia's largest customers in Southeast Asia.By January 2026, Caprez had been promoted again to vice-president of global AI infrastructure growth.A Swiss national and former professional skier and consultant, Caprez met Madison Huang while both were studying at London Business School.The links of both executives to Nvidia's relationship with Megaspeed are expected to face greater scrutiny as the company's board conducts an investigation led by a former senior US prosecutor.Megaspeed has been under US investigation since 2024 over suspicions that it was involved in diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of American export controls. The Singapore-based company purchased approximately $5 billion worth of Nvidia hardware.According to information released by the US Commerce and Justice departments on Monday, the investigation began after authorities detected suspicious activity involving the possible diversion of sensitive semiconductors.The US Commerce Department approached Nvidia in May 2025 seeking records of its direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed. The chipmaker placed the Singapore company on its restricted sales list the following month.The two departments said in a joint statement, "After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the department of commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations."In June 2025, US agents travelled to Megaspeed's premises alongside Singaporean law enforcement officials to conduct an "on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed". They also questioned Alice Huang, who was then the company's chief executive.The Justice Department subsequently took charge of the criminal investigation. The agencies said they were making details of the case public despite the usual practice of not commenting on ongoing investigations, citing public interest.Nvidia had earlier told the New York Times that it had visited Megaspeed's facilities several times, found no Chinese shareholders and detected no evidence of chip smuggling.The company has also maintained that it placed Megaspeed on its "block list" in June 2025, "prohibiting any further sales or shipments".Nvidia, representatives for the Huang family and Heller declined to comment on the latest allegations.The controversy has also drawn congressional attention, with Jensen Huang summoned to testify about Nvidia's relationship with Megaspeed at a closed-door session in December.The former CEO has agreed to appear before the House committees on Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China for transcribed interviews on December 1. Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter is expected to appear before the committees on December 2.The committee chairs, Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford, said in a joint statement on Tuesday, “We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security.”Meanwhile, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has criticised Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and his department for failing to place Megaspeed on the US blacklist. The Commerce Department has delayed new additions to the list.On Tuesday, Nvidia's board also established a new National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to supervise the company's compliance with US national security and export regulations.Megaspeed's former executive Alice Huang has also come under scrutiny over suspected links to Chinese espionage efforts. US intelligence officials reportedly believe she had a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, an allegation that, along with reports of a second relationship involving a subordinate, preceded his resignation on November 12 after 33 years at the helm of Nvidia.Megaspeed said on Sunday that Alice Huang had formally left the company on August 30, 2025, while maintaining that it had conducted a "legitimate and lawful business."Singapore's government said last week that Alice Huang had previously held three key positions at Megaspeed: chief executive, chairperson and one of its key controllers.Singapore police found insufficient evidence to establish that she had committed offences related to suspected false declarations over server purchases. However, authorities issued her a warning for knowingly providing inaccurate information that downplayed her role in the company.Singapore has also barred Alice Huang from re-entering the country, while investigations involving Megaspeed and six other individuals remain underway, according to the Home Affairs Ministry.The Singapore government said on Monday that it had agreed to continue discussions with Washington over the company.
Article Summary: Madison Huang, daughter of Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, helped shape company's response to Megaspeed probe. Her husband, Nico Caprez, also assumed a broader role in Nvidia's international business.Megaspeed has been under US investigation since 2024 over suspicions that it was involved in diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China.

Oracle CEO Mike Sicilia has acknowledged that technology companies have made mistakes in how they communicate the benefits of data centre projects to local communities, arguing that the industry needs to rely more on local voices and demonstrate tangible societal benefits if it wants to win public support. The comments made by Sicilia come as the datacenter developers face increasing scrutiny from the residents and policymakers over issues such as energy consumption, water usage and the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.According to Fortune, Sicilia said technology and data-centre companies are increasingly finding that local approvals and community acceptance have become as important as securing power supplies or advanced chips for AI projects. "It's actually not surprising," Sicilia said, noting that many technology companies have historically operated as suppliers rather than active participants in local communities.As a result, the industry is still learning how to engage with residents and local stakeholders in areas where major infrastructure investments are planned. The remarks come amid heightened debate over the economic and environmental impact of AI-driven data centres across the United States.Sicilia also stressed on the adoption of finance as a model, he noted that in community banking the regional managers made lending decisions which come from the serve the region. He added that the tech companies should also take lessons from other industries and hire heavily from the communities where they function.Healthcare could help showcase AI's benefitsSicilia suggested that healthcare may be one of the strongest examples the industry can use to demonstrate the value of AI investments. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin

How ‘Superintelligence’ may be overloading older systems

Not a cyberattack, DHS secretary says

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) secretary Markwayne Mullin has blamed ‘superintelligence’ (SI) – a term given by US President Donald Trump as a substitute for AI – for the recent outages that impacted flights, email platforms and online banking in the country. He also sent a straightforward message for Americans worried about the wave of major tech disruptions: take a breath. Mullin’s comments came on the heels of widespread digital headaches on Monday (November 16), when customers reported trouble logging into major US banks, including Wells Fargo, Chase, US Bank, and Bank of America. That same day, United Airlines was hit by a broad system outage that briefly disrupted departing flights. Last week, Microsoft 365 was hit, rendering services inaccessible.During an appearance on Fox News, Mullin said: “We just have a lot of technology thrown at us and our world runs on technology now. We used to have backup systems and the backup systems are overwhelmed by the new systems now.”He also shared a theory raised by a tech expert, not Elon Musk, who told him that (SI) may have played a role in the breakdowns – an explanation the secretary said “kind of makes sense.”According to Mullin, the expert explained that older software simply isn't built to keep pace with self-coding AI.“He said, because these programs aren’t designed to work as fast as SI is. And so when they put in a program that’s able to write codes, and it goes in and it self-fixes itself, as it starts self-fixing itself, it’s like doing a change order on a house. When you change one thing in a house, everything else starts changing. That’s a ripple effect,” Mullin said.He added: “It causes these systems to be overrun that weren’t designed to run as fast as the SI technology is today.”Defending the Trump administration’s handling of the recent tech failures, Mullin pledged to send federal resources to assist companies struggling with system breakdowns. “We are very secure, and I feel very comfortable about where we’re at,” he said.Despite the clustering of high-profile failures, Mullin pushed back against fears of a coordinated hack, calling the incidents “individually unrelated.”“I can tell you with 98% certainty we’re not seeing the cyberattack. We’re not seeing the footprints going in. We’re not seeing the footprints going out. And so, nothing points to it being connected,” the DHS secretary said.“Well, breathe. The homeland is secure. Our banking system is secure and when something like this happens, we’re able to react and react fast,” Mullin noted. Those glitches followed a rough week for critical infrastructure, including a nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) that triggered widespread flight delays and cancellations.
Article Summary: DHS secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed'superintelligence' (SI) for recent tech outages. Mullin said older software isn't built to keep pace with self-coding AI. He also pushed back against fears of a coordinated hack, calling the incidents ‘individually unrelated’

Article Title: After Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees, CEO Satya Nadella explains the decision; says: I wish I could just sit here and ...
Article Text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella : ‘Vote with your feet’

What was Microsoft’s buyout offer

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has addressed the question over the tech giant’s massive new buyout program and whether this is a sign of upcoming AI-driven layoffs, explaining that the company is reshaping how its teams work rather than simply shrinking its headcount. Speaking after Microsoft rolled out a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to roughly 60,000 workers, which is more than a quarter of its global staff—Nadella emphasized that the future of the company will look noticeably different in terms of team sizes and daily workflows.“It’s a very important question. Let’s acknowledge that there is going to be plenty of opportunity going forward. The shape of that opportunity may be different,” Nadella said, adding, “The shape of what this new thing looks like is going to be different than what it was before: team sizes and team workflows.” While Nadella stressed that he wants all 200,000-plus Microsoft employees to grow and flourish, he noted that the workforce “will have to be configured in different ways. ”According to the CEO, the voluntary buyout is designed to give employees control over their careers as the company evolves, especially for those sitting in units that have been slow to adapt.“This voluntary thing was mostly about letting everybody have more agency to get themselves into places that make sense for their economic opportunity long term.That's, I think, the key thing. I don't want to be stuck in a team that's not transforming, even inside of Microsoft. Let's face it. It's not like I can sit here and say every part of Microsoft has really got the memo," Nadella explained at The Pragmatic Engineer podcast.He added that employees who feel professionally stuck now have the option to leave on good terms, though he encouraged them to explore internal transfers first.“If you're in a team where you feel stuck professionally, you can vote with your feet. I don't want you to, because quite frankly there are many places you can go inside of Microsoft itself. I wish I could just sit here and say it'll all be the same. I cannot. And this is one of those places where I want to be as transparent about the change,” Nadella said.Chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the Voluntary Exit Offer in a memo to staff, framing it as a chance for employees already considering a move outside Microsoft to exit now with financial backing and career support. The offer applies to eligible staff at internal level 70 and below, which is a group that includes roles up to general managers and some vice presidents, across just four countries: The US, Canada, The UK and India.Unlike Microsoft’s spring retirement buyout, this offer has no age or tenure minimums and job performance is not a factor. Eligible workers have until the first week of December to decide, with departures set for the end of the year.The buyout terms match Microsoft’s standard severance package. During US layoffs earlier this year, severance included at least 60 days of base pay on the payroll and up to 39 weeks of base pay depending on seniority and tenure – giving employees at level 64 and below one week of base pay per six months of service, and those at levels 65 to 67 two weeks per six months.The VEO also covers continued stock vesting, career transition help, and healthcare coverage for a fixed period. Unlike the earlier retirement program, however, it does not include extended healthcare benefits. Individual terms are being sent via email to eligible staff, including those in India.This marks Microsoft’s second major buyout push in 2026 following waves of layoffs over the past two years. In 2025 cuts, Microsoft eliminated more than 15,000 jobs.This year, the company launched its first-ever Voluntary Retirement Program for about 8,750 US staff (senior director level and below) whose age and years of service totaled at least 70. Microsoft laid off 4,800 workers (around 2% of its workforce) in July, hitting Xbox and commercial sales hardest, followed by hundreds more cuts in September.
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says the future of the company will look noticeably different in terms of team sizes and daily workflows. Microsoft rolled out a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to roughly 60,000 workers, which is more than a quarter of its global staff.

Article Title: A Melbourne woman spent A$2,000 on four Apple gift cards at Coles, but discovered their redemption codes were scratched out; the supermarket initially refused a refund before agreeing to return her mo
Article Text:
Image Credit: AI Generated

Melbourne woman's A$2,000 Apple gift cards found with scratched-out codes

Why did Coles initially refuse to refund the money

How did Coles eventually agree to return the A$2,000

What did the ABC investigation discover about gift card fraud

How does the gift card tampering scam operate

Are Australian supermarkets taking steps to prevent the problem

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A Melbourne woman who spent A$2,000 on four Apple gift cards at Coles discovered that their redemption codes had been scratched out, leaving her unable to use the vouchers. The purchase, which initially appeared to be a way to earn extra Flybuys points, turned into a frustrating dispute after supermarket staff reportedly refused to refund the money. The retailer eventually reversed its decision and agreed to return the amount. The incident later became part of a wider ABC News investigation into tampered gift cards being sold across Australia.According to an ABC News investigation report published on May 21, 2026, Melbourne-based illustrator Georgia Perry bought four Apple gift cards from a Coles supermarket in Yarraville, an inner-western suburb of Melbourne. Each card was worth A$500, bringing the total purchase to A$2,000.Perry had purchased the vouchers on a Tuesday evening because she wanted to buy a new iPhone. An in-store promotion offering 20 times the usual Flybuys points on Apple gift card purchases also made the deal appear attractive.However, the purchase took an unexpected turn when she returned home and began opening the cards. The first voucher appeared to have no usable redemption code, with the area where the code should have been showing signs of scratching or peeling.Initially, Perry thought she might have damaged it while removing the card from its packaging.The same problem appeared on the remaining three cards. All four vouchers had their redemption codes scratched out, making them unusable for the intended purchase.Perry took the four vouchers back to the supermarket after discovering the damage. However, she told ABC News that the store staff were unwilling to help and reportedly explained that they could not take responsibility because gift cards were third-party products.She also contacted Apple for assistance. During the process, the company's helpline asked her to provide photographs of the cards, including their serial numbers. This revealed another problem, as the final digits on the cards had also been scratched out.Perry subsequently lodged a formal complaint with Coles. The supermarket confirmed receiving it and said its customer care team had responded within an hour and continued working towards a resolution.The initial response left Perry dissatisfied. She described the customer service experience as uninterested and lacking urgency. She also questioned how the cards could have reached the shop floor in that condition, particularly because the damage was not obvious while they remained attached to their cardboard packaging.The situation changed after Perry shared a video of her experience on Instagram. Her complaint attracted widespread attention, receiving more than 150,000 views by the morning after it was posted, alongside hundreds of comments from people discussing gift card fraud and consumer rights.According to ABC News, a Coles employee left Perry a voicemail confirming that a refund would be issued. Emails reviewed by the ABC team showed that the gift card supplier had deactivated the A$2,000 worth of vouchers and returned the money to Coles.The supermarket subsequently informed Perry that she was eligible for a refund and apologised for the poor experience.In an extensive investigation published on August 31, 2026, ABC News revealed that shoppers across Australia had reported buying gift cards with missing or damaged redemption codes from major supermarket chains.The investigation examined 19 reports of suspicious gift cards, many involving Apple vouchers. It reviewed customer receipts, photographs of damaged cards and correspondence with retailers, Apple and gift card distributors.The earliest reports identified by the ABC dated back to 2024. That year, a Coles customer in Perth and a Woolworths shopper in Sydney reported problems with their purchases.The ABC investigation identified another customer, Lavkesh Arora, who bought five Apple gift cards worth A$2,000 from a Coles store in the city’s eastern suburbs. Two of the cards worth A$700 combined, had missing redemption codes and digits. Another shopper, Damian Toohey, reported finding a scratched-off number on an Apple gift card purchased from Woolworths.The ABC investigation also examined how criminals could tamper with physical gift cards before returning them to supermarket shelves.Adam Parks, a former Australian representative of the US Department of Homeland Security's investigative unit, explained that the practice is commonly known in the industry as card draining.According to Parks, the process can involve people taking gift cards from shop shelves, carefully opening their packaging and recording the information needed to access the funds. They may use razor blades or hair dryers to remove the packaging without leaving obvious signs of damage.The cards are then returned to their packaging and placed back on supermarket shelves. When an unsuspecting customer purchases one, the retailer activates it at the checkout.The stolen information can then be used to monitor the card's balance and activation status. Once a customer pays for the voucher, those involved in the scam may spend its value before the buyer gets an opportunity to redeem it.This can make the fraud difficult to identify immediately. Gift cards are frequently purchased as presents, meaning some customers might not open them for weeks or months after the original transaction.Parks told ABC News that the operation becomes profitable when carried out on a large scale, with different people potentially handling the collection, tampering and use of the stolen information.The ABC investigation found that Coles had previously worked with police to address gift card tampering. Court documents revealed that a man was arrested after allegedly placing tampered Apple gift cards on shelves on at least 5 Coles stores in Sydney.Police alleged that the cards involved were worth at least A$10,200. The man was sentenced to a two-year community corrections order and a 15-month suspended sentence.Both Coles and Woolworths acknowledged the wider problem and defended their efforts to prevent it. Woolworths was trialling anti-tamper hangers and staffed stations near gift card displays in some stores.Apple had also changed its Australian gift card packaging in early 2025. The newer design included perforated edges intended to make signs of opening or interference easier to identify. Its packaging also carried a warning against buying or selling cards that appeared to have been tampered with.
Article Summary: Melbourne woman's A$2,000 Apple gift cards found with scratched-out codes. Coles initially refused to refund the money. The retailer eventually reversed its decision and agreed to return the amount. Incident later became part of a wider ABC News investigation into tampered gift cards being sold across Australia.

Article Title: Argos denied a customer in UK refund for a $500 laptop bought online, as had switched it on and activated Windows 11; two years later, he won a Court of Appeal ruling as the court upheld 'sealed-softw
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

Why did Argos refuse the refund at first

What does the sealed-software exception cover

Can retailers still deduct money for use

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Argos has been ordered to refund a customer who activated Windows 11 on his laptop. The Court of Appeal in England and Wales has ruled that switching on a computer bought online and activating its pre-installed operating system to test it does not, by itself, remove the buyer’s statutory cancellation right.According to a report by Solicitor News, the unanimous ruling rejected Argos’s reliance on the “sealed-software exception” after Dr Ebenezer Adodo sought to return a $500 Lenovo laptop in September 2024. The court held that he had bought a computer with an operating system installed, rather than sealed software sold separately. It ordered Argos to refund the price with interest, clarifying the distinction between testing an online purchase and using goods beyond what is necessary to assess them.Adodo ordered the Lenovo IdeaPad, preloaded with Windows 11, through Argos’s website on August 31, 2024. He also bought a $13 mouse pad and collected both items that day.At home, he switched on the laptop to check whether it met his needs. He found compatibility problems with software he used for his work at Leicester University. The mouse pad was also too large for his computer table.He repacked both products and took them back on September 5.Argos refused the return, citing opened packaging and the laptop having been switched on.An initial county court decision accepted Argos’s argument that the purchase was not a distance contract. On appeal, a judge found that the contract had been concluded online and awarded a refund for the mouse pad. However, that judge accepted that activating Windows 11 had broken a digital seal, preventing cancellation of the laptop purchase. Adodo then took the laptop dispute to the Court of Appeal.The Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 generally allow consumers to cancel an online goods purchase within 14 days of receiving it, without giving a reason.An exception covers sealed computer software that becomes unsealed after delivery. The appeal court interpreted that exception narrowly: the software must itself be the object of the sale, supplied on a physically sealed carrier such as a CD or USB stick.A laptop’s pre-installed operating system did not turn the computer purchase into that kind of software transaction. Activating Windows to assess the machine therefore did not extinguish Adodo’s cancellation right.The ruling does not give buyers unrestricted use of a product before returning it. Regulation 34 allows retailers to recover a proven reduction in value caused by handling beyond what is necessary to establish the goods’ nature, characteristics and functioning.Reasonable resetting costs may qualify in an appropriate case. However, Argos had not established whether such costs existed or how much they were. The court ordered interest on the laptop refund from 14 days after Adodo’s unsuccessful return attempt.
Article Summary: Dr Ebenezer Adodo tried to return a $500 Lenovo laptop in September 2024. Argos refused the return, citing opened packaging and the laptop having been switched on. The Court of Appeal in England and Wales has ruled that switching on a computer bought online and activating its pre-installed operating system does not, by itself, remove the buyer’s statutory cancellation right.

Article Title: Google launches new Gemini Notebook feature to turn research into interactive sites
Article Text:
Designed for work and study

Sharing and collaboration support

Global rollout begins

Google has rolled out a new capability for Gemini Notebook which will enable the users to transform their notes research materials and source documents into interactive websites. The feature announced by the tech giant allow users to generate websites directly from the information stored in their notebooks, making them better understand and explore complex topics. As per Google, users can simply type ‘make me a site’ in the Gemini Notebook chat and the give a description of the project they wish to create. The AI-powered tool will then create an interactive website on the basis of the sources and content.“Starting today, Gemini Notebook can turn your sources into interactive sites to help you quickly make sense of complex information. To get started, simply type “make me a site” in your Gemini Notebook chat along with a description of what you want to build for work or study,” said Google in a blog post.Google said the feature can be used across a variety of educational and professional scenarios. Examples include creating visual explainers for exam preparation, such as interactive periodic tables and historical timelines, as well as interactive dashboards for analysing data like quarterly sales performance.Users can also generate project management trackers to organise tasks and deadlines. The company says the goal is to help users quickly make sense of large amounts of information by presenting it in a more engaging and interactive format.Google adds that once the website is created, users can then open it in a new browser tab and interact with it or share it with others. The latest feature also adds the capabilities of Gemini Notebook which goes beyond summarisation and research assistance. Also, this new tool helps in turning collected information into an interactive experience which can be explored and also shared more easily.Google said the new feature is rolling out globally on the web for Gemini Notebook users aged 18 and older, including subscribers to Google Workspace. The company added that support for the mobile app will arrive at a later date. The update is part of Google's broader push to make AI tools more useful for productivity, education and knowledge management, enabling users to convert static research materials into interactive websites with a simple text prompt.

Article Title: Sale of an oceanfront mansion in Golden Beach for record $69.5 million, has the town speculating about Jeff Bezos as the likely buyer after ...
Article Text:
Rumours point to Jeff Bezos

Record sale for Golden Beach

The house

Why buyers use LLCs

A second home near the first

A note of caution

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jeff Bezos’ Florida portfolio

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos may have added a beach house to his $237 million Miami compound, though nothing has been confirmed. According to a public records search by Fortune, a Delaware LLC paid $69.5 million in September for a 17,500-square-foot oceanfront estate at 255 Ocean Boulevard in Golden Beach, an exclusive town in Miami-Dade County. Public records list the buyer as Meridian Coast LLC, a structure that keeps the person behind the purchase out of view. Agents and other sources in town have pointed to Bezos, The Real Deal reported, and say he would likely use the property as a beach house. Bezos has not publicly confirmed the deal, and his representatives did not immediately respond to Fortune’s request for comment.While the buyer has not been officially identified, local real estate agents and sources cited by The Real Deal have linked the purchase to Bezos. The report noted that the billionaire has not publicly confirmed any involvement in the transaction, and representatives for Bezos did not immediately respond to Fortune's request for comment.The property is located roughly a 30-minute drive from Bezos' existing real estate holdings in Indian Creek, the exclusive island community often referred to as the "Billionaire Bunker." Bezos already owns a sprawling Miami-area compound valued at about $237 million, according to Fortune.Industry experts noted that it is increasingly common for ultra-wealthy buyers to route purchases through LLCs and trusts to enhance privacy and security. Ken DeLeon, founder of DeLeon Realty, previously told Fortune that such structures help prevent ownership records from being directly tied to high-profile individuals.The transaction set a new record for a single-family home sale in Golden Beach, according to The Real Deal. The waterfront mansion features seven bedrooms, 12 bathrooms, a guesthouse, swimming pool, spa and approximately 100 feet of ocean frontage. Property records reviewed by Fortune show the home was initially listed in February for $88.5 million before the asking price was later reduced to $79.5 million. The final sale price of $69.5 million still established a benchmark for the affluent coastal enclave.The sale set a record for a single-family home in Golden Beach, according to The Real Deal. The house has seven bedrooms and 12 bathrooms, plus a guesthouse, a pool, a spa and 100 feet of water frontage. It came on the market in February at $88.5 million, and the price was later cut to $79.5 million, public records reviewed by Fortune show.Buying through LLCs and trusts has become more common among the ultrawealthy, who increasingly see public attention as a security risk. Ken DeLeon, founder of DeLeon Realty in Palo Alto, told Fortune earlier this year that the aim is to make sure even someone digging through ownership records cannot easily link a property to the person behind it.The Golden Beach house is only about a 30-minute drive from Bezos’ compound in Indian Creek, known as the “Billionaire Bunker,” a 300-acre man-made strip of land that has drawn many of the ultrawealthy. Mendel Fellig of the Mendel Fellig Group at Compass told Fortune that, at Bezos’ level, owning another home nearby isn’t redundant. A buyer with an excellent waterfront home may still want direct access to a private stretch of beach, he said, and Golden Beach is one of the few places in Miami that offers that, making the second property “almost an amenity in itself. ” He added that assembling a portfolio gives such buyers different residential experiences while securing properties that are increasingly hard to replace.Not everyone is convinced. Devin Kay of Douglas Elliman told Fox Business that recognisable names tend to get attached to blockbuster deals when a buyer’s identity is hidden. He said South Florida’s pool of billionaire buyers has expanded considerably, with international business owners, hedge fund executives, technology founders and multigenerational families quietly buying some of the region’s most valuable property.If Bezos is the buyer, the house would join a portfolio he began building after leaving Seattle for Miami in 2023. He said then that he wanted to be closer to his parents and to Blue Origin’s operations at Cape Canaveral. The move has also paid off at tax time. Florida has no state income or capital gains tax, and Fortune previously reported, citing a Forbes calculation, that Bezos saved an estimated $1 billion in 2024 alone, compared with about $954 million in Washington State capital gains tax he would have owed on his Amazon stock sales that year.
Article Summary: A Delaware LLC paid $69.5 million in September for a 17,500-square-foot oceanfront estate in Golden Beach, an exclusive town in Miami-Dade County. Public records list the buyer as Meridian Coast LLC, a structure that keeps the person behind the purchase out of view. Agents and other sources in town have pointed to Bezos, and say he would likely use the property as a beach house. Bezos has not publicly confirmed the deal, and his representatives did not immediately respond to Fortune’s request for comment.

America’s largest bank JPMorgan Chase has now revealed that the temporary software bug led to the delays in some customer transactions on November 16, disrupting some consumer banking services and triggering reports of outages across parts of the US banking system. According to a report by CNBC, the bank stated that the issue was linked to a software bug in its on-premise hardware systems, resulting in some transactions taking longer than usual process. The lender also stressed that the customers were still able to access their accounts and funds and said that there was no evidence that the disruption was related to any cyber attack.While outage reports surfaced across several major US banks, JPMorgan said the issue was not systemic. The bank noted that other financial institutions could experience slower transactions only if they were involved in payments or transfers with JPMorgan, meaning any knock-on effects were linked to interactions with the bank's systems rather than a broader banking-sector outage. CNBC reported that there was no indication that bad actors were involved in the incident and no sign that a common software bug was simultaneously affecting multiple banks“There is no evidence it is cyber-related,” a JPMorgan spokesperson said in a statement to CNBC. “This is not a systemic issue — other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us,” the spokesperson said. “We’re working diligently to resolve this by the end of the day today.”Customers across several of the largest banks in US ran into trouble trying to access their accounts online on Monday (November 17). According to outage tracking website Downdetector.com, users reported that services were down or experiencing issues across multiple major financial institutions and payment platforms, including Bank of America, Chase, JP Morgan, US Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle.As per a report by AP, some Chase users trying to log in were met with an error notice stating: “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”The problems follow major outages last week, when a Microsoft email outage disrupted businesses. Coverage also notes that a FAA outage halted commercial air traffic, making the bank problems the third major tech disruption in days. JPMorgan has given no sign that its issue is connected to either.

Article Title: FBI warns companies in the US and across the world; names AI hacking tool criminals are using to attack financial services; suggests dos and don'ts
Article Text:
FBI recommends organizations take the steps below to improve their security posture:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Hackers are increasingly deploying autonomous artificial intelligence tools to execute high-speed cyberattacks across the United States and around the globe, according to a flash cybersecurity advisory issued by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. The warning highlights a wave of recent intrusions targeting major sectors—including government, defense, telecommunications, law, technology, and finance—with major fallout already documented across South Korea’s financial industry and among thousands of customers of American IT firm ConnectWise.At the center of the FBI’s alert is Artex, an open-source, AI-powered penetration testing platform originally designed to probe network defenses. By linking Artex to frontier large language models from companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, as well as open-source and foreign AI models, threat actors have been able to automate the discovery and exploitation of basic security flaws. "Since at least August 2026, a variety of malicious cyber actors have used Artex to conduct campaigns targeting organizations globally across multiple sectors, including financial services, government, technology, defense, semiconductor, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, telecommunications, and legal industries," said FBI in its report.While federal officials noted that Artex-driven intrusions are often "noisy"—generating high volumes of network traffic that can set off security alarms—the software operates at a pace that routinely outstrips human response times. In several observed cases, attackers progressed from initial targeting to full system compromise in under three hours.Once aimed at a target, the software rapidly scans networks for low-hanging vulnerabilities, such as weak configurations, missing multi-factor authentication, or exposed passwords. Upon securing a foothold, the tool autonomously navigates internal systems to harvest sensitive databases, mailboxes, and credentials.Since Artex debuted publicly in July, its capabilities have been tied to several high-profile breaches. In South Korea, attackers leveraged the platform against multiple financial institutions lacking basic protections like multi-factor authentication, resulting in the theft of personal records belonging to at least 68,000 individuals. "As of early November 2026, researchers identified over 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX console instances, with total deployments likely significantly higher when including systems behind firewalls or in private networks," says FBI.The FBI also corroborated earlier intelligence from Microsoft detailing how threat actors—believed by Microsoft to be operating out of China—used Artex to infiltrate IT management provider ConnectWise. Through that breach, the hackers accessed the Microsoft 365 cloud environments of at least 2,250 ConnectWise customers to exfiltrate data.Although the creator of Artex has since transitioned the software to a closed-source model in an effort to curb abuse, the FBI cautioned that earlier open-source versions remain widely circulated and easily accessible online. Compounding the threat, careless operational security by the hackers themselves has left hundreds of active Artex instances exposed on the public internet without password protection. Just last week, cybersecurity researchers discovered numerous unprotected deployments online—including the exact system used to orchestrate the attacks against South Korea—potentially leaving powerful, turnkey hacking infrastructure open to anyone who stumbles across it.• Restrict cloud administration, network device management, application publishing interfaces (Kudu/SCM endpoints), hypervisors, backup platforms, and other sensitive services to trusted networks,private connectivity, or dedicated administrative paths.• Disable basic publishing authentication where not required; restrict access to deployment and publishing credentials; restrict SCM access to approved management networks or deployment infrastructure.• Consider deployment models such as run-from-package that reduce direct modification of deployedapplication files.• Establish governance around public IP allocation; require architecture review before workloads or management interfaces are exposed directly to the internet.• Move enterprise applications behind Zero Trust access solutions to eliminate external exposure where feasible.* Put guardrails around high-impact business APIs: rate limits, recipient limits, transaction thresholds, abuse controls appropriate to function; alert when application operates materially outside normal volume.* On partner and employee portals, alert on sequential lookups and unusually high numbers of records accessed per session; apply rate limits to affected endpoints; enforce server-side authorization for access to customer records and limit responses to fields required for the operation.
Article Summary: Hackers are increasingly deploying autonomous artificial intelligence tools to execute high-speed cyberattacks across the U.S. and around the globe. The warning highlights a wave of recent intrusions targeting major sectors. At the center of the alert is Artex, an open-source, AI-powered penetration testing platform.

Article Title: US government proposes new rules for Green Cards; tells companies: American Workers are the best in the world, rule change will ensure they are …
Article Text:
US government proposes new rules for Green Cards; tells companies: American Workers are the best in the world

What changes are being proposed to Green Card rules

Companies that laid off US workers could face restrictions

Nurses and physical therapists could also face new requirements

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When will the proposed Green Card rules take effect

The US government is proposing stricter rules for companies sponsoring foreign workers for employment-based Green Cards. The US Department of Labor says the changes will ensure that qualified American workers get the first opportunity to apply for high-skilled, high-paying jobs before companies turn to foreign workers. “American Workers are the best in the world, and they deserve the first and best job opportunities,” Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said while announcing the proposal. He added that the rule change would put American workers “first in line” for such jobs.The proposal seeks to overhaul the Permanent Labor Certification programme, also known as PERM. It is the first major update to the programme in nearly 20 years.For the unaware, PERM is an important step for many employment-based Green Card applications under the EB-2 and EB-3 categories. Before sponsoring a foreign worker for permanent employment, companies generally have to show that they could not find qualified US workers for the position and that hiring the foreign worker would not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of American workers. PERM approval itself does not grant a Green Card.One of the biggest changes involves how companies advertise jobs. The Labor Department wants employers to move away from print-based advertisements and use modern recruitment methods. Under the proposal, companies would have to advertise vacancies through their websites, online job portals and social media platforms. They may also use job fairs and campus recruitment.Employers would have to keep job advertisements open for at least 90 calendar days. If they normally advertise similar positions for a longer period, they would have to follow that longer period. The department says this would give qualified American workers more time to learn about vacancies and apply.The proposal would also require companies to use the same recruitment channels and methods for PERM positions that they use for similar jobs that do not require labour certification. Employers would have to make genuine efforts to consider qualified US applicants and provide job-related reasons if they reject them.The proposed rules also target companies that lay off American employees while seeking to sponsor foreign workers. Under the proposal, employers would be barred from filing a PERM application if they had laid off US workers in the same or a similar occupation at the relevant work location during the previous two years.If a company lays off American workers after filing a PERM application, it would have to consider potentially qualified laid-off employees for the position. This requirement could continue until the related Form I-140 immigrant petition is approved or the case reaches a final decision.Employers would also have to inform the Labor Department, and the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) where applicable, about such layoffs within five business days.The Labor Department has proposed ending the administrative exemptions under a system known as Schedule A. At present, certain occupations, including professional nurses and physical therapists, can bypass the usual labour market test under Schedule A. The exemption also covers certain individuals with exceptional ability in the sciences, arts and performing arts.If the proposal is adopted, employers seeking to sponsor foreign workers in these categories would also have to test the US labour market and consider qualified American applicants.The changes are not final yet. The Labor Department has invited the public to submit comments on the proposal for 60 days after its publication in the Federal Register on November 17.The proposal is part of the US administration's wider efforts to tighten employer-sponsored immigration pathways and strengthen protections for American workers. If finalised, the changes could make the PERM process more demanding for companies seeking to sponsor foreign employees for permanent residency in the US.
Article Summary: US Department of Labor says the changes will ensure that qualified American workers get the first opportunity to apply for high-skilled, high-paying jobs. The proposal seeks to overhaul the Permanent Labor Certification programme, also known as PERM. It is the first major update to the programme in nearly 20 years.
